subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: List strategies for dealing with new words
Guess the meaning of a word from its context

tf.s: Guessing from context means using the words around the new word.
tf.why: The context gives clues to the meaning.

tf.s: You must always look up every new word in a dictionary.
tf.why: You can also guess from context or sometimes ignore the word.

tf.s: Guessing from context saves time and keeps you reading.
tf.why: You do not need to stop for every word.

tf.s: Ignoring a new word is never a possible strategy.
tf.why: Ignoring a word is one of the strategies students listed.

tf.s: A dictionary is useful when a word is essential and the context gives few clues.
The words before and after an unknown word can give clues.
tf.why: They often show what the word means.

tf.s: A vocabulary notebook helps you record and remember new words.
tf.why: Writing words down helps you learn them.

tf.s: After guessing a meaning, you should not check it in the sentence.
tf.why: Test your guess in the sentence to see if it makes sense.

tf.s: Context means the sentences and text around a word.
tf.why: Yes, context is the words around it.

tf.s: Stopping to look up every word makes reading faster.

boxes.q: Which strategy uses the words around a new word?
'The test was simple; everyone finished in five minutes.' 'Simple' means...
boxes.why: Everyone finished quickly, so it was easy.

boxes.q: Why is guessing from context useful?
'After running 10 km, he was exhausted and lay down.' 'Exhausted' means...
boxes.why: Running far and lying down show he was tired.

boxes.q: 'The ancient castle was built 900 years ago.' 'Ancient' means...
boxes.why: 900 years ago tells you it is old.

boxes.q: 'The room was spotless; there was no dirt anywhere.' 'Spotless' means...
Where can you write new words to remember them?
boxes.why: A vocabulary notebook keeps new words together.

boxes.q: What should you do after guessing a meaning?
boxes.why: Check that the meaning makes sense.

boxes.q: 'She was elated when she heard she had passed.' 'Elated' means...
boxes.why: Passing an exam makes you happy.

Using the words around a new word

mcq.q: Which three strategies did students list for dealing with new words?
o: Ignore it, use a dictionary, guess from context
Copy it, delete it, shout it
Draw it, sing it, spell it
Skip the page, close the book, stop reading

mcq.q: What can help you guess the meaning of a new word?
o: The words before and after it
mcq.why: Clues are in the surrounding words.

o: The words and sentences around a word
mcq.why: Context helps you understand a word.

mcq.q: When is a dictionary better than guessing?
o: When the word is essential and the context gives few clues
mcq.why: Use a dictionary for important words you cannot guess.

mcq.q: 'The road was so congested that we waited an hour in traffic.' 'Congested' means...
mcq.why: Waiting an hour in traffic is the clue.

mcq.q: 'Although he was wealthy, he lived in a small house and spent little.' 'Wealthy' means...
mcq.why: 'Although' shows a contrast with spending little.

mcq.q: 'The instructions were ambiguous, so nobody knew what to do.' 'Ambiguous' means...
mcq.why: Nobody knew what to do, so they were unclear.

mcq.q: Why is it sensible to test each possible meaning in the sentence?
o: To see which meaning makes sense
mcq.why: The right meaning fits the sentence.

mcq.q: 'Unlike his noisy brother, Sami is reticent.' Which clue helps you guess that 'reticent' means quiet?
mcq.why: 'Unlike' shows Sami is the opposite of noisy.

mcq.q: Why can stopping to use a dictionary for every word be a problem?
o: It slows you down and breaks your reading
mcq.why: Too many stops make it hard to follow the text.
